# HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA

A chronic inflammatory condition that typically involves occlusion, rupture, abscess formation and infection of hair follicles as well as secondary infection of apocrine glands/surrounding tissues. Lesions most often occur in the intertriginous areas (axillae, inguinal and anogenital) in is associated with smoking and obesity. There is a 40% genetic predisposition for hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) and is often accompanied by pain, malodor, and drainage. Cultures are negative 50% of the time and often are polymicrobial with S. epidermidis and S. aureus most isolated. The Hurley Staging System is often used
to determine severity of HS.

Therapy generally consists of treatment of comorbidities that can exacerbate HS, avoidance of triggers, pain management, wound care, and topical/oral antimicrobials. Hormonal agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery can also be used to treat certain patients. Biologics may be considered in Stage II-III HS.

## Consult Dermatology in all cases.

## Hurley Staging System:

Stage I: recurrent nodules and abscesses with minimal scarring
Stage II: limited number of sinuses and/or scarring within a body region
Stage III: multiple or extensive sinuses and/or scarring

## Duration of Therapy:

Treatment is typically for 12 weeks but may require longer durations in certain cases. Metronidazole should only be used for a maximum of 6 weeks to avoid neurologic toxicity.

## Interventions for All Patients:

Smoking cessation, weight loss, avoidance of triggers, and pain management should be part of all treatment plans. Consult Dermatology for use of hormonal agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

## Optional Topical Treatment, May be Used in Addition to Oral Therapies Below:

Chlorhexidine gluconate 4% liquid topically wash affected area q24h ($) [M]
< OR >
Benzoyl peroxide 10% soap topically wash affected area q24h ($) [M]
< ADD ON THERAPY FOR FLARES - MUST USE IN ADDITION TO ONE OF THE AGENTS ABOVE>
Clindamycin 1% solution topically to affected areas q12h prn for flares ($) [M]

## Stage I-II Initial Treatment:

Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks
< OR >
Minocycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks

## Stage III Initial Treatment and Stage I-II Failure of Oral Doxycycline:

Clindamycin 300 mg PO q12h for 12 weeks ($) [H,O]

## Stage II-III Failure of Oral Clindamycin:

Moxifloxacin 400 mg PO q24h ($)[R,DI] for 12 weeks
<AND>
metronidazole 500 mg q8h ($) [DI] for 6 weeks
<AND>
rifampin 300 mg PO q12h ($) [DI,O] for 12 weeks
